home.title: MiYa — Apple Watch health report in plain words
home.description: MiYa explains what your Apple Watch measures — HRV, resting heart rate, workouts, ECG — in plain words. Free, no account; data stays on your iPhone.
home.tagline: Your Apple Watch keeps measuring. MiYa tells you what the numbers mean.
home.lead: Heart rate, HRV, blood oxygen, steps, workouts, ECG — MiYa turns them into a report you can read like a story. Free, no account, and everything is calculated on your iPhone.

features.p: One sentence on how charged up your body is, what kind of movement suits today, and the reasons behind it.
Tap the “?” next to any metric to see what it is, an everyday comparison, and how to read it.
Recovery, Strain, Stress and Battery scores use your own baseline, not someone else's average.
The Apple Watch app shows today's recovery, stress and battery; a watch face widget keeps the battery one glance away.
No account, no servers, no analytics, no ads. MiYa only reads from Health and never writes to it.
English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語 and Español — it follows your iPhone's language.

home.note: MiYa is not a medical device and does not diagnose any condition. Scores are estimates relative to your own history. If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness or palpitations, stop exercising and seek medical care.
home.art: A ray of light leaves an Apple Watch, passes through a prism and splits into four beams that end at a heart, a battery, footprints and a stopwatch.

intro.h: From your wrist to a sentence you understand

chain.p: Heart rate, HRV, blood oxygen, steps and workouts, all day.

intro.termsH: Words you'll see, in plain language

terms.d: How much the gap between heartbeats varies. Higher than your usual usually means you're well rested.
Your heart rate while still. Lower than your usual usually means recovery is good.
0–100: how ready your body is today, from HRV and resting heart rate against your own baseline.
How hard your heart worked today, from time spent at higher heart rates.
How tense your heart rate looked while you weren't exercising. It can't tell stress from coffee.
Energy left: charged by recovery, drained by strain and stress through the day.
Your own normal, from the past weeks. Every score compares you with it, not with others.
An estimate of fitness: how much oxygen your body can use at full effort.
Z1 is a stroll, Z5 is a sprint. Workouts show how long you spent in each.
Recordings from the ECG app shown as waveforms, with Apple's classification. Not a diagnosis.

map.lede: See it by part, or by when in the day you'd open it.

cats.q: Answers: is my heart working harder or easier than usual?
cats.short: Resting heart rate, HRV, blood oxygen and ECG, with what each change means.
cats.body: Long-term trends for resting heart rate, HRV, blood oxygen, breathing rate and walking steadiness. Each number has a plain sentence underneath, like “6 fewer beats a minute than before, so your heart is working more efficiently.” ECG recordings are shown as waveforms.

cats.q: Answers: should I push or rest today?
cats.short: Recovery, Strain, Stress and Battery, scored against your own baseline.
cats.body: Four 0–100 scores. Recovery uses HRV and resting heart rate; Strain uses time at higher heart rates; Stress uses heart rate while you weren't exercising; Battery combines them through the day. Days with too little wear are left out instead of guessed.

cats.q: Answers: am I moving as much as I think?
cats.short: Steps, distance and patterns, plus a weekly walking route.
cats.body: Steps and distance over weeks and years, your most active days and months, and streaks against a goal set from your own median. Your real steps move a character along a different route each week.

cats.q: Answers: what did each workout actually do?
cats.short: Routes, heart rate zones and which workouts recharge you most.
cats.body: Every workout with its GPS route, heart rate zones and stats, plus patterns like which kind of workout is followed by your best recovery the next day.

day.p: Open MiYa or glance at your watch: one sentence on whether to push or take it easy, and why.
Low battery and low recovery mean an easier session will do more good.
Route, heart rate zones and how hard it was compared with your usual.
Resting heart rate and HRV over 90 days tell you more than any single day.

numbers.lede: Two charts with example numbers. Hover or tap for values.
numbers.sample: Example numbers for illustration, not real data.
numbers.hrvCaption: The band is your usual range. Days above it suggest you're well rested; a run of days below it is a cue to take it easier.
numbers.recCaption: The same score, read with the three bands the report uses.
numbers.heroNote: HRV on the best day, compared with the baseline

privacy.title: MiYa Privacy Policy
privacy.description: MiYa collects no data. Health data is read and processed only on your iPhone; optional recordings go only to devices you own.
privacy.updated: Last updated: November 16, 2026 · Applies to MiYa for iPhone and Apple Watch
privacy.intro: MiYa collects no data about you. The developer has no servers, no accounts and no analytics, so there is nowhere for your data to be sent. This page explains what MiYa reads, where it is kept, and the one optional feature that moves data between your own devices.

ul: MiYa reads steps, heart rate, HRV, blood oxygen, workouts, ECG and similar records from the Health app, only after you allow it.
All calculations happen on your iPhone. The results are stored in a database file on the iPhone.
MiYa never writes to or changes anything in Health.
The report is excluded from iCloud backup, as Apple requires for health data.

sections.p: The iPhone sends a small summary (today's scores and weekly goals) to your Apple Watch through Apple's built-in iPhone–Watch connection. It never passes through any server run by the developer.

ul: Off by default. If you turn it on, your Apple Watch records audio and passes it to your iPhone.

Speech is turned into text on the iPhone with Apple's on-device recognition. If you set up your own computer for transcription, recordings are sent only to the address you enter — a computer on your home network or reached through your own private network (such as Tailscale). The developer never receives recordings or text.
If you turn on Record Places, MiYa notes where you were for each recording. Locations stay on your devices.
Recordings can pick up other people. Follow local laws and ask for consent when required.
No third-party analytics, advertising or crash-reporting SDKs.
No selling or sharing of data — there is no data to sell or share.
App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected.

sections.p: In MiYa, open About & Privacy and choose Delete Data on This Device to remove the report. Recordings can be deleted one by one in the recordings list. Deleting the app removes everything it stored. Turning off MiYa's access in the Health app stops any further reading.
MiYa is not directed at children and collects no data from anyone.
If this policy changes, the new version will be posted on this page with a new date. Questions: {email}

support.title: MiYa Support
support.description: Help with MiYa: syncing Health data, scores, languages, deleting data, and how to contact the developer.
support.intro: Answers to common questions. If yours isn't here, email the developer — replies usually come within a few days.

faq.a: MiYa can only show what is in the Health app. Check Settings → Privacy & Security → Health → MiYa and allow the data types, then tap Sync Again. An Apple Watch gives the most data; iPhone-only step data also works.

faq.q: Why don't my scores match another app?
faq.a: Recovery, Strain, Stress and Battery are calculated by MiYa against your own baseline, so they won't match other apps exactly. The trends should line up.

faq.q: Some days have no recovery score.
faq.a: Recovery needs HRV and enough wear time. On days you wore the watch only briefly, resting heart rate isn't reliable and is left out.

faq.q: How do I change the language?
faq.a: MiYa follows your iPhone's language. You can also pick a language in the report menu, or under Settings → MiYa → Language.
In MiYa, open About & Privacy and choose Delete Data on This Device. Recordings are deleted one by one in the recordings list. Deleting the app removes everything it stored.
No. MiYa does not diagnose any condition. If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness or palpitations, seek medical care.

support.contactNote: Please don't send health data or screenshots containing personal information unless you're comfortable sharing them.
